component.title: Papyrus
component.description: Papyrus is a single-tenant agent runtime that an organization deploys in its own environment as a FIPS-mode container image on Amazon Linux 2023 or an Azure VM appliance. It runs named, signed agents and workflows over the organization's documents and connected systems, signs people in through the organization's OpenID Connect provider (Microsoft Entra ID is one option), takes its configuration from a reviewable papyrus.yaml, keeps an append-only audit trail it can export over OTLP, and routes consequential external actions through human approval.

controls.title: Account Management
controls.statement: Papyrus creates no local user accounts or passwords; every person is an identity from the organization's OpenID Connect provider or Microsoft Entra ID, configured in papyrus.yaml, and authority comes only from the declared Papyrus roles, from token or directory-group claims mapped in papyrus.yaml, or from Papyrus role assignments. There is no first-run setup page: the first System Owners are named in papyrus.yaml (identity.owners) and receive the role when they first sign in. Only a System Owner (never an API key) can grant or revoke roles, the last System Owner cannot be revoked, and every grant and revocation is written to an append-only event table. With SCIM 2.0 provisioning on, a person the directory deprovisions or deactivates loses access on their next request. Automation uses API keys: service identities with no roles that name the workflows they may run and expire after 1 to 365 days (default 90).
controls.customer: Own the account lifecycle in the identity provider (proofing, approval, periodic review, removal), name the first System Owners in papyrus.yaml, and review Papyrus role assignments and API keys on the organization's cadence.

evidence.note: principalFromClaims and group mappings; grantConfiguredOwner grants identity.owners at sign-in; withDirectory checks SCIM status per request
Append-only role events, last-System-Owner guard

gap.description: A person who holds System Owner through a Papyrus role assignment keeps access while SCIM reports them deprovisioned (intended as break-glass), and there is no administrator action to end a person's active sessions.
gap.remediation: Limit the SCIM bypass to accounts named in papyrus.yaml and audit each use; add a System Owner action to revoke a person's sessions.

controls.title: Access Enforcement
controls.statement: Every protected HTTP route authenticates the caller server-side and rejects principals that hold no Papyrus role; administrative, integration, approval, audit and owner-only operations check the specific role on the server before acting. Until a System Owner accepts the current Terms of Service and Privacy Policy in the app, only sign-in, the terms and health routes answer. MCP servers, imported APIs and API keys are scoped to the caller's tenant, and an API key is admitted only to start runs of the workflows it names and read the runs it started. Named agents run only from an active, signed revision; within a session an agent may use any tool the deployment offers, and whether a tool call needs a person's approval is decided by the tool's permission policy and, for MCP tools, the administrator's classification.
controls.customer: Assign Papyrus roles in Entra according to organizational need-to-know.

evidence.note: requireRole/requireAnyRole on routes; TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED gate (LEGAL_EXEMPT)
assertSession requires an active signed revision; beforeTool enforces budgets
Tool permission policies (allow/ask) per tool and MCP classification

verification.note: Integration operations require Entra application roles
Rejects an authenticated user without an observability role
API keys refused everywhere except starting and reading their own workflow runs
People without Integration.Manage see only verified servers and no settings

gap.description: Agent sessions, their messages, the AgentFS Library and generated artifacts are owned by the tenant, not by the person who created them. Any signed-in person holding any Papyrus role can list and read every session, Library file and artifact in the deployment.
gap.remediation: Record an owner on each session and Library namespace, enforce owner or explicit-share checks in the session, workspace-file and artifact routes, and add tests for cross-user denial.

controls.title: Information Flow Enforcement
controls.statement: Papyrus enforces fixed flow rules in code: agent workspace commands run with network access denied; repository imports and package installs are downloaded by the server, never the sandbox, and nothing in them runs; credentials are resolved by trusted runtime code and never passed to models or workspace processes; MCP tool results are labeled as external content. Outbound requests made for workflow HTTP steps, link previews, MCP servers and repository imports pass an egress gate: with egress.allowedHosts set in papyrus.yaml only listed hosts (names or *.suffix) are reached, and on the disconnected profile nothing outside the boundary is reached until it is listed.
controls.customer: Set PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_DENYLIST and PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_INTERNAL_HOSTS to match the authorization boundary, and enforce egress policy at the network layer.

evidence.note: assertEgressAllowed: allow-list, default deny on disconnected
Workflow HTTP targets checked against the gate
Link previews checked against the gate
MCP servers checked against the gate
Every redirect hop checked; links and paths outside the target skipped

verification.note: Default deny on disconnected, listed hosts, wildcard matching
Redirect hosts checked against the allow-list

gap.description: Model gateway, identity provider discovery and Sentry connections do not pass the egress gate (they are configured endpoints), and the gate does not pin the resolved address, so a host that changes its DNS answer between check and connect could reach an internal address.
gap.remediation: Route every outbound connection through the gate and connect to the address that was checked.

controls.title: Separation of Duties
controls.statement: The agent can propose but cannot approve: approveProposal, denyProposal and executeAction are rejected at the agent tool layer, and approval routes require a human Entra session holding Papyrus.Action.Approve. Workflow approval steps addressed to a person or group can be answered only by that person, a member of that group, or a System Owner, never by the person who started the run. Authority-weakening policy changes wait for a Governance principal (System Owner, or Security.Manage plus Action.Approve).
controls.customer: Assign Papyrus.Action.Approve, Papyrus.Security.Manage and Papyrus.System.Owner to different people according to organizational separation-of-duties policy.

evidence.note: FORBIDDEN_AGENT_TOOLS lists approveProposal, denyProposal, executeAction
mayAnswerApproval: assigned approvals exclude the requester
requireGovernance and governed_changes approval
approveProposal requires Papyrus.Action.Approve

verification.note: Keeps approval and execution out of the agent's tools
Requester cannot approve their own addressed request, even as an approver

gap.description: Action proposals and governed changes do not check that the approver differs from the person who proposed or requested them, so one person holding the approving roles can approve their own request. Unaddressed workflow approval steps can be answered by the run's initiator.
gap.remediation: Refuse approval when the approver's object ID equals the proposer or requester for action proposals, governed changes and unaddressed workflow steps, with an explicit single-operator override recorded in the audit log.

controls.title: Least Privilege
controls.statement: Papyrus splits authority into roles (integration view and manage, security manage, action approve, audit view and system owner) and checks the narrowest one per operation; Papyrus.System.Owner implies all of them. API keys hold no roles. The container runs as a non-root user, and workspace commands run with the data directory unreadable and network denied.
controls.customer: Grant the narrowest role that fits each person, limit System Owner assignments, and do not run the container privileged.

evidence.note: ENTRA_APP_ROLES and OBSERVABILITY_APP_ROLES
hasAppRole: System Owner implies every role
Role descriptions declared on the Entra app
USER nonroot in the runtime stage

verification.note: System Owner role is treated as all portal permissions

gap.description: Possession of any role, including narrow ones such as Papyrus.Audit.View, grants access to the shared agent workspace: all sessions, chat, Library files and artifacts. Workspace access is not itself a separately assignable privilege.
gap.remediation: Introduce a distinct workspace-use role or per-session ownership (see ac-3) so that narrow roles do not carry workspace access.

controls.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
controls.statement: Papyrus accepts no passwords, so interactive logon attempts and lockout are handled by the identity provider. Every completed and failed sign-in callback is written to the audit trail with the client address. Workflow webhook secrets are 256 random bits made by the server, and invalid, expired, revoked and rotated API keys all receive the same 401.
controls.customer: Configure Entra smart lockout, Conditional Access and sign-in risk policies for the tenant.

evidence.note: auth.sign_in success and failure audit records on the OIDC/Entra callback
Uniform 401 for bad keys

verification.note: Bad and missing signatures get 401; a rotated-away secret stops working
Missing, malformed, revoked or rotated-away keys get the same answer

controls.title: System Use Notification
controls.statement: With security.notice set in papyrus.yaml, Papyrus shows the system use notice before sign-in (dow for the standard DoD notice and consent banner, or the organization's own text from a file) and starts sign-in only after the person consents. Each acknowledgement is recorded in the audit trail with the notice's digest and the client address.
controls.customer: Choose the notice text approved for the system and set security.notice.

evidence.note: DOW_NOTICE, systemNotice; login refused without the acknowledged digest; auth.notice_acknowledged record
Notice screen before the sign-in button

controls.title: Concurrent Session Control
controls.statement: Each person may hold at most three portal sessions at once by default (security.sessions.concurrent); a new sign-in ends the oldest beyond the limit.
controls.customer: Set the limit the organization requires.

controls.title: Device Lock
controls.statement: After 15 minutes without activity (security.sessions.idleMinutes) the portal signs the person out and returns to the sign-in screen, and the server ends the session independently, so an unattended browser requires re-authentication through the identity provider.
controls.customer: Apply operating-system screen locks on endpoints.

controls.title: Session Termination
controls.statement: Portal sessions are recorded on the server. Each sign-in opens a session that ends after 15 minutes without activity, after 12 hours however active it is, or on sign-out, which ends it on the server so a copied cookie stops working (security.sessions in papyrus.yaml sets the limits). The signed cookie carries only the session identifier and identity; each request is checked against the session record, and ending a session is audited.
controls.customer: Set identity-provider token lifetimes and sign-in frequency; choose session limits in papyrus.yaml that meet the organization's policy.

evidence.note: Server-side sessions: idle limit, maximum lifetime, concurrent cap, end on sign-out

controls.title: Security and Privacy Attributes
controls.statement: With security.classification set in papyrus.yaml, every screen, including sign-in and the Terms page, carries the system-high classification banner at the top in the standard colours (UNCLASSIFIED through TOP SECRET//SCI).
controls.customer: Set the system-high classification; apply marking to documents and media under the organization's marking policy.

controls.title: Event Logging
controls.statement: Papyrus writes one append-only audit trail of security events: successful and failed sign-ins, sign-outs, sessions ended for inactivity or age, acknowledgement of the system use notice, every refused request (401 and 403) with its route, acceptance of the Terms, and audit export tests. Separate append-only records cover role grants and revocations, every MCP tool call and MCP administrative change, API key lifecycle, policy decisions, configuration at each start, integration and action-ledger events, and agent signatures and evidence.
controls.customer: Decide which additional events the organization requires and collect Entra sign-in logs from Microsoft.

evidence.note: papyrus_audit_events: one schema, append-only
Sign-in, sign-out, notice, terms and access.denied records
Session end records

verification.note: Lifecycle events are appended and the chain verifies
Records who classified an MCP tool

gap.description: Document downloads, session and workflow deletions, and agent tool calls are recorded in their own stores or not at all, rather than in the unified audit trail.
gap.remediation: Write these events to the unified audit trail.

controls.title: Content of Audit Records
controls.statement: Unified audit records carry a sequence number, an ISO 8601 UTC time, the action, the outcome (success, failure or denied), the actor and the person an agent acted for, the target, the client network address, user agent, request ID and session ID, and event detail without secrets or document content. MCP call records add session, workflow, tool classification, approval ID, duration and a SHA-256 of the arguments.

evidence.note: AuditEvent fields; auditRequest takes the socket address, never a forwarded header

verification.note: Key create/replace/delete does not leak secret values into audit events

controls.title: Audit Log Storage Capacity
controls.statement: Audit records are kept in the Papyrus data directory and, when audit.otlp is configured, delivered to the organization's collector; records written while the collector is unreachable are sent when it returns, and the backlog is shown on the Audit page.
controls.customer: Size the data volume and the collector's storage for the retention period the organization requires.

evidence.note: Durable export cursor and backlog

gap.description: Papyrus does not watch free space on the data volume or alert when it runs low.
gap.remediation: Add capacity monitoring and an alert.

controls.title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
controls.statement: System Owners and Audit Viewers review the trail on the Audit page: search by person or action, filter by outcome and time range, read each record in full, and export the filtered list as CSV or JSONL. The same records are sent to the organization's OpenTelemetry collector (OTLP/HTTP, with optional CA and mutual TLS) for review in its SIEM, at least once, resuming after an outage; the page shows the export's health and can send a test record.
controls.customer: Set review cadence, alerting and escalation, and correlate Papyrus records with Entra and host logs in the organization's monitoring system.

evidence.note: OTLP exporter: durable cursor, retry with backoff, TLS and mTLS
Audit page: filters, detail, CSV/JSONL export, export status

controls.title: Time Stamps
controls.statement: Papyrus writes audit timestamps as ISO 8601 UTC strings taken from the host clock.

controls.title: Protection of Audit Information
controls.statement: Audit tables are append-only at the database layer: triggers abort UPDATE and DELETE on the unified audit trail and on role, configuration, MCP, integration and model event tables; integration and action-ledger events are additionally SHA-256 hash-chained. With OTLP export configured, every record is also held by a collector outside the Papyrus host.
controls.customer: Restrict host and database-file access, protect backups, and copy audit records to independently controlled immutable storage.

evidence.note: No-update/no-delete triggers and verifyEventChain

States that a host or database administrator can replace local state

verification.note: verifyEventChain reports a valid chain after lifecycle changes

gap.description: Triggers detect changes made through the application only; anyone with write access to the database file can rewrite local records, and the unified trail is not hash-chained or signed. Off-host export mitigates this only when configured.
gap.remediation: Chain and sign the unified trail with a key held outside the data directory and verify it on a schedule; require OTLP export on classified deployments.

controls.title: Audit Record Generation
controls.statement: Audit records are generated server-side at the enforcement points themselves: the proposal approval and denial paths, the single MCP call path, role assignment changes, API key management and policy enforcement. controls.title: Baseline Configuration
controls.statement: Papyrus ships one container image: Amazon Linux 2023 minimal with OpenSSL's certified FIPS provider forced on, running as a non-root user with no browser engine, scanned in CI against the DISA STIG profile for Amazon Linux 2023. Runtime configuration comes from papyrus.yaml, a reviewable file in which secrets appear only as file or environment references, and its digest and effective settings are recorded at every start. Three deployment profiles (commercial, government, disconnected) set network posture.
controls.customer: Document the approved deployment configuration: host OS, network, Entra registration, model endpoint, storage and the Papyrus image digest.

evidence.note: Build and runtime stages, nonroot user, dod target

gap.description: The baseline is not fully reproducible: base images are referenced by tag rather than digest, apk packages are not version-pinned, and several Python packages in the runtime image (pypdf, pypdfium2, reportlab, pillow) are unpinned.
gap.remediation: Pin base images by digest and pin apk and pip package versions, with an automated update process that opens reviewed changes.

controls.title: Configuration Change Control
controls.statement: In-application changes that weaken policy become digest-checked governed changes that apply only after a Governance principal approves them, and an approval is refused if the change's digest or expected version no longer matches. Papyrus software updates are announced by exact image digest from an allowed repository and installed only when a System Owner applies them or within an owner-configured maintenance window.
controls.customer: Operate organizational change control for deployment configuration, infrastructure and when updates are applied.

evidence.note: propose/approve with digest and expected-version checks

verification.note: Approved change commits atomically; a stale approval is rolled back without relaxing rules
Accepts only exact digests from allowed repositories and applies only when asked or in the window
A relaxation waits as a governed change and applies only on approval

controls.title: Access Restrictions for Change
controls.statement: Configuration endpoints require specific roles on the server: Integration.Manage for model gateways, MCP servers, imported APIs, package mirrors, browser and mainframe settings and branding; System Owner for role assignments, updates, license activation and skill approval; Governance for governed changes. Model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin.
controls.customer: Control access to the host, container runtime, data directory, secret stores and deployment pipeline.

evidence.note: requireRole checks on configuration routes; requireSecretTransport
requireGovernance

controls.title: Configuration Settings
controls.statement: Configuration is validated at startup and fails closed: papyrus.yaml is checked against its schema (unknown keys and bad values stop startup), an identity provider is required, persistent mode requires an HTTPS public origin, the license named in license.file must verify for this deployment, and the former development and license bypasses are refused. Every start records which file was used, its digest and each effective setting with where it came from, and flags a change from the previous start.
controls.customer: Choose values appropriate to the authorization boundary and verify them at deployment. In Azure Government or other national clouds, set PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINT, PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_RESOURCE, PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_DNS_SUFFIX and PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_RESOURCE; they default to Azure commercial endpoints and are not derived from PAPYRUS_ENTRA_CLOUD.

controls.title: Least Functionality
controls.statement: The runtime image contains no browser engine. The Papyrus agent has no general shell: native programs run only through structured executors (Python, Pandoc, LibreOffice) with fixed executables. MCP has no stdio transport. The public scheduler CRUD surface is not exposed, and removed legacy connectors read back as retired and cannot be activated or executed.
controls.customer: Expose only ports 80/443 (and SSH if needed), and disable integrations and model endpoints the organization does not use.

controls.title: System Component Inventory
controls.statement: A generator produces an SPDX 2.3 SBOM of every package in the pnpm lockfile, checked for drift by the pre-commit hook, and the container workflow generates a CycloneDX SBOM of the built image.
controls.customer: Inventory the host OS, container runtime, reverse proxy, model endpoints and other infrastructure in the boundary.

controls.title: Signed Components
controls.statement: Release images are signed with Cosign keyless signing in GitHub Actions. On the Azure Marketplace appliance the updater runs cosign verify against a pinned signer identity and issuer before pulling an update and installs nothing if verification fails; the Marketplace image pipeline verifies the signature and build provenance of the container digest before baking it.
controls.customer: On self-hosted deployments, verify the image signature and digest before deployment.

evidence.note: cosign verify with PAPYRUS_UPDATE_SIGNER_IDENTITY before install

verification.note: Update service accepts only exact digests from allowed repositories

gap.description: Signature verification exists only on the Marketplace VM update and image-build paths; the shell updater has no automated test, and other deployment paths do not verify signatures in this repository. The Azure template (deploy/azure/main.bicep) references ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus:0.1.1 by tag, a different repository from the one CI publishes (ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus/papyrus). Two workflows (container.yml and container-multiarch.yml) sign images for the same repository while the updater trusts only the container.yml identity.
gap.remediation: Settle on one signing workflow and identity, reference images by digest from the published repository in every deployment template, add an automated test for the updater verification step, and document signature verification for every supported deployment path.

controls.title: System Backup
controls.statement: Papyrus keeps its state in the data directory (agent.db, mastra.db, jobs.db, observability.db, secrets.db and AgentFS) and documents which files must be backed up together and that the local master key must be backed up separately. It provides no backup tooling.
controls.customer: Back up the data directory consistently, store the master key and Key Vault recovery separately, and test restoration.

evidence.note: Lists the databases to back up and master key handling

controls.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
controls.statement: People authenticate only through the organization's OpenID Connect provider or Microsoft Entra ID. Before sign-in starts, a configured system use notice must be acknowledged. Sign-in uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), single-use state and a nonce; ID tokens are verified against the provider's published keys for issuer, audience, expiry and nonce. Multi-factor and PIV/CAC requirements are enforced by the identity provider, not by Papyrus.
controls.customer: Require MFA or phishing-resistant authentication through Entra Conditional Access.

evidence.note: startLogin, completeLogin, verifyEntraToken, completeBrokeredLogin

verification.note: Interactive login requests the expected scopes per national cloud
An API key is not accepted as an Entra sign-in

gap.description: Papyrus does not itself require multi-factor or certificate-based authentication (it trusts the identity provider's policy) and cannot accept client certificates (CAC/PIV or SIPR tokens) directly.
gap.remediation: Optionally require MFA or smart-card authentication methods in the token (amr/acr), and support mutual TLS with NSS PKI where the enclave requires it.

controls.title: Identifier Management
controls.statement: Papyrus identifies people by Entra object ID and tenant ID and creates no identifiers of its own for people. API keys receive a random 12-hex-character identifier, and each deployment has its own deployment ID.
controls.customer: Manage identifier issuance and reuse policy in Entra ID.

controls.title: Authenticator Management
controls.statement: API key secrets are 32 random bytes, shown once with cache-control no-store, and stored only as an HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the deployment secret, so a copied database cannot be used to call the API. Keys expire, can be rotated (the old secret stops immediately) and revoked. Integration settings reject inline passwords, tokens and keys and store only credential references, and model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin. The pre-commit hook scans staged changes for private keys and common token formats.
controls.customer: Manage Entra authenticators (MFA methods, certificates, client secrets) and rotate API keys on the organization's schedule.

The only unauthenticated route for other systems is a workflow webhook (/hooks/<id>): it answers only for a published workflow with a webhook trigger, requires a signature made with the server-generated secret, and only starts that workflow with the event as its input.

controls.title: Incident Handling
controls.statement: Papyrus provides no incident handling capability or plan. Its audit and observability records are inputs to the deploying organization's process.
controls.customer: Maintain and exercise an incident response plan covering the Papyrus deployment, including revoking roles, API keys and connector credentials and preserving audit databases.

controls.title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
controls.statement: The repository has workspace-wide TypeScript type checking and a Vitest suite for the server covering identity, authorization, MCP, secrets, sandboxing and approvals. CI runs type checking and a fixed subset of tests (scoped workflows, mainframe guardrails, policies, execution records, channel linking and offline evaluations), and a local pre-commit hook runs secret, contract and compliance-drift checks plus security-invariant tests when related files change.

evidence.note: CI typecheck and the tests it runs

gap.remediation: Run the full server test suite and pnpm compliance:check in CI on every pull request and make them required checks.

controls.title: Information in Shared System Resources
controls.statement: Papyrus databases are opened with SQLite secure_delete, so content removed from them is overwritten rather than left in free pages. Each agent workspace runs in its own sandboxed process with a temporary materialized workspace.
controls.customer: Use volume encryption and sanitize media under the organization's procedures.

evidence.note: secure_delete on agent.db
secure_delete on session and trace stores

gap.description: Deleting a session does not remove every copy of its content (workspace files, traces, embeddings), and there is no administrator purge for spillage.
gap.remediation: Add a cascading purge with verification.

controls.title: Denial-of-Service Protection
controls.statement: Request bodies are read under fixed byte ceilings and refused with 413 beyond them; workflow webhooks are rate-limited per webhook and take bodies of at most 1 MB; pending sign-ins are capped; and outbound workflow requests time out after 15 seconds with bodies limited to 256 KiB.
controls.customer: Provide network-layer DoS protection and rate limiting at the reverse proxy or gateway.

evidence.note: body() and rawBody() byte limits
MinuteRateLimiter
Per-webhook delivery limit

verification.note: Refuses an oversized chat body

gap.description: Rate limits are in memory and keyed on the socket address; behind the appliance's nginx proxy every client shares one address, and the limiter clears all windows once it tracks 10,000 keys. The cap of 256 pending sign-ins can be exhausted by unauthenticated requests, blocking sign-in for up to 10 minutes.
gap.remediation: Key limits on a trusted forwarded client address, bound memory without clearing all windows, and rate-limit /api/auth/entra/login per client instead of a global cap.

controls.title: Boundary Protection
controls.statement: Workflow HTTP steps, link previews, MCP servers and repository imports pass one egress gate: HTTPS, no embedded credentials, refusal of hosts that resolve to loopback, private or link-local addresses unless listed as internal, and, when egress.allowedHosts is set (required on the disconnected profile), only listed hosts. Redirects are re-checked hop by hop. Workspace commands have no network access. On the Marketplace appliance the container is published only on 127.0.0.1 behind nginx.
controls.customer: Place the deployment behind the organization's firewalls and proxies, restrict inbound access to 443, and set the egress denylist and internal-host list.

evidence.note: assertWorkflowHttpTarget
mcpFetch applies the same check and redirect: manual
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:${PAPYRUS_PORT}; nginx proxy
Deployment vault created with publicNetworkAccess Enabled

verification.note: Address classification, denylist and internal-host rules
Refuses private addresses and plain HTTP to public hosts

gap.description: The address check resolves DNS separately from the connection that follows, so a host that changes its DNS answer between the two can reach an internal address. The deployment Key Vault is created with public network access enabled.
gap.remediation: Connect to the address that was checked (pinned lookup) for all outbound requests, and support private endpoints or firewall rules for the deployment Key Vault.

controls.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
controls.statement: Persistent mode refuses to start without an HTTPS public origin. The daemon can terminate TLS itself with a TLS 1.2 minimum, and the Marketplace appliance's nginx edge allows only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 and sends HSTS. Portal cookies are Secure under HTTPS. Outbound connections to MCP servers, workflows and imported APIs require HTTPS except for hosts the organization explicitly lists as internal.
controls.customer: Provide certificates, TLS termination and cipher policy that meet organizational requirements.

evidence.note: Persistent deployments require an HTTPS PAPYRUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN
createHttpsServer with minVersion TLSv1.2
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 and HSTS

verification.note: Rejects plain HTTP to non-internal hosts

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
controls.statement: The local secrets master key must be a separately provisioned 32-byte file that is not group- or world-writable and is opened without following symlinks; the server never generates it. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, the portal secret, Entra client secret and model and provider keys are kept in a deployment Key Vault (RBAC mode, purge protection, 90-day soft delete) with only the VM's managed identity granted access, and each reader is limited to its own secret-name prefix. License authority public keys are supplied by configuration or baked into the DoD image.
controls.customer: Provision, back up and protect the master key and portal secret; manage Entra and TLS keys.

evidence.note: Master key checks
Core vault and purpose-prefix read guard
Vault properties and single role assignment
Connector credential key derived as SHA-256 of the portal secret

verification.note: Fails closed with missing, insecure or incorrect master keys
Each caller reads only its own secrets; references refused without an Azure identity

gap.description: There is no rotation or key-versioning support for the portal secret or the local master key. Encryption keys for connector credentials are derived with a single SHA-256 of the portal secret, so changing that secret makes stored values unreadable. The Key Vault uses the Standard (software-protected) tier.
gap.remediation: Introduce versioned data-encryption keys with a proper KDF, a re-encryption procedure for rotation, and an option for HSM-backed keys.

controls.title: Cryptographic Protection
controls.statement: The image runs OpenSSL with Amazon Linux 2023's certified FIPS 140-3 provider (CMVP #5438) forced on, and Papyrus refuses to start if FIPS mode is not active or MD5 is still allowed. Stored credentials use AES-256-GCM; cookies, API key hashes and webhook signatures use HMAC-SHA-256; hash chains use SHA-256.
controls.customer: Where FIPS 140 validated cryptography is required, run on a validated module and terminate TLS on validated infrastructure.

evidence.note: Startup refuses to run unless getFips() is 1 and MD5 is refused
AL2023 with openssl-fips-provider-certified, FIPS forced

gap.description: Signatures and MACs use P-256 and SHA-256 rather than the CNSA suite (P-384, SHA-384) that national security systems may require.
gap.remediation: Move Papyrus-generated signatures and MACs to CNSA algorithms while still verifying existing ones.

controls.title: Mobile Code
controls.statement: Papyrus runs no agent-built code in the browser. HTML and SVG artifacts are served as attachments with a sandbox CSP (default-src 'none'), so they cannot run in the portal's origin.

evidence.note: Active artifact content served as attachment with sandbox CSP

verification.note: HTML artifacts are sandboxed attachments; passive content is inline

controls.title: Session Authenticity
controls.statement: The portal session cookie is HMAC-SHA-256 signed with the deployment secret, compared in constant time, and set HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure and with the __Host- prefix under HTTPS. OIDC state and nonce are random 32-byte values held server-side, single-use and expiring after 10 minutes; MCP OAuth sign-ins are likewise single-use, bound to the initiating person and checked against the discovered issuer. Once an HTTPS origin is configured, request headers cannot change the origin used for redirects or cookies.

evidence.note: portalCookie, verifyPortalCookie, pending login state
10-minute single-use pending sign-ins with issuer check
deriveOrigin

verification.note: Refuses a callback from another person, a reused state and a different issuer
HTTPS origin authoritative over Host headers
Signed cookie carries only the authority-bearing identity

controls.title: Protection of Information at Rest
controls.statement: Papyrus encrypts secrets at the application layer with AES-256-GCM and per-record associated data: model gateway keys in a separate 0600 secrets database under a separately provisioned master key; and connector, imported-API and MCP credentials bound to their owner. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, platform secrets are stored there and configuration files hold only references. SQLite databases are opened with secure_delete, so deleted rows are overwritten rather than left in free pages.
controls.customer: Encrypt the volume that holds the data directory and its backups, and manage those keys.

evidence.note: secrets.db encryption and file permissions
Owner-bound AES-256-GCM connector credentials
Key Vault storage of platform secrets

verification.note: Encrypted persistence, tamper rejection and cross-profile binding
Shared MCP token stored encrypted and never returned
bootstrap.json holds only references

gap.description: Agent sessions, Library documents, audit records and traces are stored in unencrypted SQLite and AgentFS files; their confidentiality at rest depends on volume encryption the deploying organization provides.
gap.remediation: Require and verify an encrypted volume for the data directory on classified deployments.

controls.title: Process Isolation
controls.statement: Commands the Papyrus agent runs in its workspace run in a separate worker process under landstrip (Landlock and seccomp on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) with writes limited to a temporary materialized workspace, the Papyrus data directory unreadable and network denied. The worker validates and resolves the effective policy before starting the command and refuses to run if the write root, network restriction or data-directory denial is not in effect; unsupported platforms run no workspace commands. Credential-like environment variables are removed before the command starts.
controls.customer: Run on a Linux host with Landlock enabled and do not run the container privileged.

evidence.note: landstrip policy, validate/resolve checks, fail-closed exits
Worker launch and sensitiveEnvironmentKey stripping
Read-confinement check of the resolved policy

verification.note: Fails closed without OS isolation; strips credential-like environment values; rejects cwd traversal
Reports landstrip isolation and refuses escaping working directories
Rejects snapshots that include daemon data or parent roots

controls.title: Flaw Remediation
controls.statement: Beag Labs publishes fixes as new signed images. A deployment learns of a release through an HMAC-signed, timestamped webhook with replay protection, and a System Owner applies it or allows it to apply within a maintenance window; the Marketplace updater verifies the image signature before installing.
controls.customer: Set patch windows, test updates and apply them within organizational timeframes.

evidence.note: verifyWebhook, announce, apply, maintenance window
Signature verification and install

verification.note: Signature over timestamp and body, replay refusal, window-limited auto-apply

gap.description: Beag Labs has no documented flaw remediation timeframes by severity, and no published security advisory or vulnerability disclosure process (no SECURITY.md).
gap.remediation: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and severity-based remediation SLAs, and announce fixed vulnerabilities in release notes.

controls.title: System Monitoring
controls.statement: Papyrus records agent traces and logs in a separate observability database readable by System Owners, Audit Viewers and Security Managers, writes structured JSON warnings to standard output, and can send errors to a customer-supplied Sentry DSN. Security events are written to the unified audit trail and exported to the organization's collector over OTLP when configured. The container health check verifies that the landstrip sandbox enforces its boundary; it does not check that the HTTP service is answering.
controls.customer: Collect container output and audit data into the organization's monitoring platform and alert on it.

evidence.note: Observability trace and log routes
Optional Sentry reporting
HEALTHCHECK
Health check probes landstrip write confinement only

verification.note: Role-gated access to traces and logs

controls.title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
controls.statement: Releases are referenced by image digest and signature-verified before the Marketplace updater installs them. Governed changes are re-hashed at approval and refused if the digest differs. Integration and action events are hash-chained.
controls.customer: Verify image digests and signatures on deployment paths other than the Marketplace appliance.

evidence.note: Exact digest references only
CHANGE_TAMPERED digest check

verification.note: Stale approvals roll back

controls.title: Information Input Validation
controls.statement: Request bodies must be JSON objects under per-route byte limits; required strings are length-bounded; policy rules are validated against a fixed schema; outbound addresses are validated before use; and workflow webhook payloads are signature-checked over the exact raw bytes before they are parsed.

evidence.note: body(), rawBody(), requiredString(), boundedInteger()
validateRules
verifyWebhook over the raw body

verification.note: Fails closed for missing context and invalid rules
Bounds session IDs and chat bodies

controls.title: Error Handling
controls.statement: Errors are returned as JSON with a code and a per-request ID. Known error types map to specific status codes, sign-in error pages do not echo request input, the browser connection address is masked in error text, and imported-API credentials are redacted from errors.
controls.customer: Configure log handling so diagnostic output is not exposed beyond administrators.

evidence.note: Central error mapping with requestId; INTERNAL_ERROR branch

verification.note: A cancelled sign-in page does not echo anything from the address

gap.description: Unexpected exceptions are returned to the client as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the exception's message text, which can disclose internal details.
gap.remediation: Return a generic message for unmapped errors and log the detail server-side under the request ID.

controls.title: Provenance
controls.statement: Container images built from main are signed with Cosign and receive a GitHub build provenance attestation. Dependencies are locked in pnpm-lock.yaml and installed with --frozen-lockfile in CI, and the pnpm version is pinned with a hash in packageManager.
controls.customer: Retain the image digests and attestations for deployed releases and verify them at intake.

evidence.note: cosign sign and actions/attest-build-provenance
Locked dependency graph
packageManager pnpm pinned with hash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

gap.description: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable version tags rather than commit SHAs, and base images and OS and Python packages in the Dockerfile are not pinned, so build inputs are not fully traceable.
gap.remediation: Pin all Actions to commit SHAs and pin image and package inputs (see cm-2), recording them in the provenance attestation.

programGaps.title: No third-party assessment or penetration test
programGaps.description: No 3PAO assessment, independent security assessment or penetration test of Papyrus has been performed. All statements in this file are derived from the source repository and its automated tests.
programGaps.remediation: Commission an independent penetration test of the application and appliance, then a 3PAO assessment against the target baseline, and track findings in the POA&M.

programGaps.title: Controls not verified in an authorized hosting environment
programGaps.description: Papyrus has not been deployed or assessed within a FedRAMP-authorized or DoD Impact Level authorized boundary, and holds no ATO. The DoD image variant only changes the default Microsoft cloud and embeds the offline license key.
programGaps.remediation: Deploy a reference instance in an authorized environment and verify each control there with a sponsoring agency.

programGaps.title: Vulnerability scanning and remediation SLAs not formalized
programGaps.description: CI performs no dependency, static or image vulnerability scanning; there are no severity-based remediation timeframes and no published vulnerability disclosure policy.
programGaps.remediation: Add scanning to CI (see ra-5), publish a disclosure policy, and adopt remediation SLAs such as those in the FedRAMP continuous monitoring guidance.

programGaps.title: Incident response and contingency planning owned by the deploying organization
programGaps.description: Papyrus ships no incident response plan, contingency plan, or backup tooling. Each deploying organization must cover Papyrus in its own IR and CP documentation, and Beag Labs has no published process for notifying customers of product security incidents.
programGaps.remediation: Publish customer-facing guidance for IR and backup/restore of a Papyrus deployment and a Beag Labs product security incident notification process.

programGaps.title: Security tests and compliance checks not enforced in CI
programGaps.description: CI runs type checking and a subset of tests; most security tests and the compliance drift check run only locally through a pre-commit hook that can be bypassed. The generated compliance/ssp.md states that these checks also run in CI.
programGaps.remediation: Run the full test suite and pnpm compliance:check as required CI checks, and correct the SSP text until they do (see sa-11).

programGaps.title: License signing-key custody outside assessment scope
programGaps.description: Licenses are signed offline with Beag Labs' Azure Key Vault keys (beag-master, beag-dev). Custody of and access to those keys is not documented here.
programGaps.remediation: Produce a control description for the license signing keys, including custody, access and rotation.

programGaps.title: Agent tool lists do not limit tool use
programGaps.description: Within an active agent session any tool the deployment offers may be used; the tools listed in an agent's signed revision record intent but are not enforced. Approval prompts, budgets and channel approvals still apply.
programGaps.remediation: Where an enclave requires per-agent least functionality, restore enforcement of the signed tool list or restrict the deployment-wide tool set.
